headline: Last session: Indian equity markets snapped 2-week gains amid elevated crude oil prices and persistent FPI selling

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 26 October.

why: Elevated crude oil prices dragged Indian equity shares to weekly losses.
Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) withdrew ₹48,056 crore from equities in October so far.
Selling pressure in auto, FMCG, and IT sectors dragged benchmark indices down earlier in the week.
Geopolitical developments and global macroeconomic concerns continue to weigh on market sentiment.
whatHappening: On the last trading day, Sensex closed down 125 points with Nifty settling near 22,600, snapping two weeks of gains.
FPI outflows from Indian equities crossed ₹48,000 crore in October amid high crude oil prices.
Primary market momentum stays strong with five IPOs preparing to raise nearly ₹2,600 crore.
Silver prices recorded a significant correction, falling to ₹1.9 lakh from earlier highs of ₹4.2 lakh.
summary: In the last trading session, Indian markets snapped a two-week winning streak as Sensex and Nifty ended lower due to surging oil prices. Heavy FPI outflows of over ₹48,000 crore in October continue to weigh on domestic equities. Stock markets are closed today for the weekend and will reopen on Monday, 26 October.
